recommended_next_phase: Phase 149O.20J.4 -- Class-B Full Ancestor-Chain Verification Repair Independent Verification. Must independently reproduce the historical early-stop behavior, independently re-derive the contract-defined ancestor boundary, prove the repaired implementation checks every relevant ancestor (writable grandparent/higher ancestors, ACL-only, effective-GID-only, symlink/error fail-closed), prove Git and Protected Root share equivalent complete-walk semantics, verify J-1/J-2/J-3 remain closed, verify zero consumers, and verify the verifier remains outside HMIC scope. Phase 149O.20K (HMIC source-scope contract evolution) must not begin until 149O.20J.4 passes. Not started, not authorized by this phase.
summary: Phase 149O.20J.3 -- Class-B Full Ancestor-Chain Verification Narrow Repair: repaired B-149O.20J.2-1, the shared _ancestor_chain_safe primitive's early-stop defect independently re-confirmed (not newly discovered) by 149O.20J.2 -- the walk previously stopped at the first ancestor proven non-writable and never examined any ancestor above it, so a writable grandparent behind an already-safe parent passed COMPLIANT undetected. Re-derived the security consequence from HBDC-001 directly: removing/renaming a directory entry requires write access on its containing directory, not the entry itself, so a writable grandparent lets the agent rename/replace a proven-safe parent's directory entry outright, defeating the early-stop design's implicit 'permanent wall' assumption. Reproduced the historical defect first via an ad hoc script against the live pre-repair source, then formalized by extracting (via ast, not a hand-copied rewrite) the exact pre-repair _ancestor_chain_safe function node from git show 8429765d:<path> (the 149O.20J.2 close-idle commit) and executing it directly against a grandparent(agent-writable)/parent(0o500,proven-safe)/state(0o500) fixture: safe=True, diagnostics contain exactly one entry (the safe-parent boundary marker) -- the writable grandparent never inspected, confirming the defect. Reconstructed HBDC-REQ-017/020's exact normative text and confirmed neither 149O.20A nor 149O.20H's Protected Root topology names an intermediate admin-owned trust anchor between Protected Root and the filesystem root; 149O.20H section 11's own original design text explicitly proposed the early-stop rule, and this phase determines that rationale was a design error refuted by its own directory-entry-replacement mechanics (already half-identified by 149O.20J.2 section 5's own observation). Boundary independently derived: the only contract-supportable stop point is the actual filesystem root. Repaired _ancestor_chain_safe: removed the early return on a locally-safe result, replaced with an ancestor_safe diagnostic entry and continued walking; indeterminate ancestors no longer short-circuit either, but force the overall result to INDETERMINATE (never COMPLIANT) if any occur along the full chain; the loop-guard-exceeded path now fails closed (INDETERMINATE) instead of falling through to now-unreachable stale tail logic. No other function or module changed -- hatp_environment_lock_verifier.py and hatp_class_b_conformance.py confirmed byte-unchanged via git diff --name-only, and both Protected Root (_check_ancestor_chain) and trusted-Git resolution (_resolve_trusted_executable_with_effective_access) confirmed via source inspection to call the exact same _ancestor_chain_safe symbol -- no divergent walker exists. Created a new 27-test independent module, tests/test_phase_149o_20j_3_class_b_full_ancestor_chain_verification_narrow_repair.py: 27/27 passed, covering historical reproduction; writable-grandparent and 5-level multi-level-matrix attacks (every level independently tested); a safe-full-chain positive case (stubbing the region outside the test's own constructed fixture as a deterministic admin-controlled boundary, since tmp_path itself is unavoidably agent-writable on any real test host and a genuine full-depth positive case cannot rely on the real filesystem above it); ACL-only and effective-GID-only higher-ancestor authority (the latter composed end-to-end with J-2's real _current_agent_identity, proving the two repairs compose correctly); symlinked/error/indeterminate higher-ancestor fail-closed handling; a static AST proof that the repaired function's locally-safe branch contains no early return; Git/Protected-Root shared-primitive equivalence; the read-only guarantee (before/after mode-bit snapshot plus a re-run of the module's own forbidden-mutation-attribute AST scan); J-1/J-2/J-3 regression; aggregator/environment-verifier byte-stability; zero-consumer and HMIC-25-scope non-binding re-confirmation; and status-vocabulary stability. Two pre-existing test assertions that documented the early-stop design as intended behavior (149O.20J's own test_deep_ancestor_writable_beyond_immediate_parent_is_caught and 149O.20J.2's own test_git_deep_ancestor_acl_only_grant_bounded_by_first_safe_boundary) are deliberately left unmodified as historical evidence, mirroring 149O.20J.1's own precedent for its superseded getegid assertion, and now fail as expected -- not regressions; both scenarios are re-proven with corrected assertions in the new module. One first-party 149O.20I unit test (test_ancestor_chain_safe_boundary) was updated like-for-like: its original fixture's safe boundary sat directly under tmp_path, which the repaired full-chain walk would now also (correctly, but spuriously for the test's own intent) inspect; updated to stub the region outside its own fixture as an admin-controlled boundary, using the same technique as the new module, while retaining its original positive assertion. Real-host result unchanged: verify_class_b_topology_conformance() returns NON_COMPLIANT (Protected Root absent), before/after git status byte-identical confirming zero mutation. Zero production authority consumers of the three verifier modules reconfirmed via fresh repository-wide search. Fresh extraction of the live _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES constant confirms exactly 25 entries, none of the three verifier module names present. Fast Green delta from a git-stash clean baseline, verified via sorted FAILED-list diff: exactly 6 transient dirty-working-tree self-checks (cleared by this phase's own commit) plus the 2 intentionally-superseded historical assertions plus 1 unrelated pre-existing xdist worker-ordering flake in test_backend_cli.py -- zero delta attributable to the ancestor-chain repair itself; the clean post-commit re-run is cited as the canonical test_results.fast_green value. Broad sweep (pytest -k 'class_b or hbdc or hmic or 149o_20'): the same 8-item delta (6 dirty-tree + 2 superseded), restricted to the narrower selector; zero other delta. CBV-S1: VERIFIER REPAIR IMPLEMENTED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION REQUIRED -- HMIC SOURCE-SCOPE BINDING STILL PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. CBV-S10: unchanged, still NOT CLOSED. B-149O.20J.2-1: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. J-1/J-2/J-3 remain independently closed, not reopened. Class-B remains CONTRACT VERIFIED -- VERIFIER REPAIRED NON-AUTHORITATIVELY -- NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. This phase does not authorize real provisioning, certification, activation, HMIC scope evolution, or readiness integration. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_3_CLASS_B_FULL_ANCESTOR_CHAIN_VERIFICATION_NARROW_REPAIR.md documenting the baseline, blocking finding, historical reproduction, requirement/boundary derivation, repair implementation, full attack-matrix verification, regression results, governance close checks, and repair verdict. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20J.2 to a new stacked Previous Phase entry) and CHANGELOG.md. Recommended next phase: Phase 149O.20J.4 -- Class-B Full Ancestor-Chain Verification Repair Independent Verification -- not authorized by this phase.
